page: Microsoft Azure E112ibs_v5 is an isolated, premium storage-capable server instance belonging to the EIBSv5 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration features 112 dedicated virtual CPUs, derived from 56 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on external block storage. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 108538.83 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17915.0, both falling into the top 25% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with read-only small block cached memory bandwidth reaching 5839.55 GB/sec and large block uncached read bandwidth at 335.8 GB/sec. In cryptography tests, the processor demonstrated top-tier performance, scoring 94803.53 on the PassMark CPU encryption test. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1693.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1899.69, placing it in the average tier.

The absence of local storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents an architectural tradeoff, requiring reliance on network-attached block storage for data persistence. However, the high memory capacity and dense vCPU count offer qualitative resource efficiency for memory-bound and multi-threaded workloads. The server is suited for database operations, as evidenced by a PassMark database score of 30672.16 and a Redis SET throughput of 96.47 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale language model prompt processing.
